correctness.rationale: Dimca–Ibadula–Măcinic Theorem 2.2 gives exactly the three complex incidence types, corresponding to 0, 1 or 3 concurrent classes. The order-three Latin square of mixed incidences reduces by relabelling to k=i+j: put the first row and column in order 0,1,2 and the remaining symbols are forced. If only one class is concurrent it can be labelled first. Each mixed point becomes a three-edge exceptional star; within each class one retains a line-pair triangle or replaces a concurrent triple by a three-edge star. The mixed incidence connects the graph, the exceptional curves meet distinct tangent directions in ordinary nodes, and the line valences are at least four. Thus all components are stable rational components and the vertex/edge/genus counts are 18/36/19, 19/36/18 and 21/36/16. Independent construction and direct integer Smith forms give nonunit lists (5,15,15,45,45,135), (3,45,45,135,405), and (3,9,9,9,9,27,27,27), with reduced determinants 307546875, 332150625, 387420489. These verify all exponents and the disappearance of 5-torsion. The conditional geometric component-group conclusion follows by the semistable graph comparison with unit edge thickness.
residual_risks: The replay checks the explicit finite graph matrices, not the complex geometric classification, which is sourced separately. This is not a single flat genus-preserving family or an assertion in other characteristics.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: This is an isomorphism, not just a numerical match: send A_i,B_j,C_k to (i,0),(j,1),(-k,2) in F3². Send concurrent-class exceptional vertices to horizontal lines, and T_ij to the affine line through (i,0) and (j,1), whose third point is (-i-j,2). The nine points and twelve affine lines realize the Hesse flex–line incidence, including every edge. This exact coverage applies to t=3 only.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification over the geometrically realizable complex net types, not an arbitrary list of graphs. The ordinary-node-preserving resolution turns concurrence into a specific local graph change; the full Smith lists show that 5-primary torsion disappears and the 3-power structure changes, facts not encoded by the incidence census or a single graph's Jacobian. The supported new comparison includes both distinct non-Ceva rows.
residual_risks: The Ceva row is not credited as an independently new exact invariant, and the comparison does not assert a flat degeneration between curves of different genera.
